prompt: In OSIsoft security Pattern 3, what crosses into the DMZ from the control network?

options.text: PI to PI carrying data only, with no user queries crossing the boundary
All PI Vision user sessions
Remote desktop for engineers
AF SDK clients querying the plant server

explanation: Pattern 3 is a DMZ with PI to PI carrying data only; no user queries cross the boundary.

options.text: A trusted domain in the DMZ, or very specific firewall rules
Switch every user to explicit logins with blank passwords
Create an open PI Trust for all IP addresses
Use Anonymous authentication

scenario: A new DMZ Data Archive must authenticate business users with Windows accounts, but the firewall blocks the DMZ from the corporate domain controllers.
explanation: OSIsoft noted firewalls block Kerberos to domain controllers and listed "a trusted domain in the DMZ" or "very specific firewalls rules". Explicit logins, open trusts and Anonymous all weaken security.

prompt: With a Waterfall unidirectional gateway, how do business users work with PI data?

options.text: They interact bi-directionally with enterprise replicas, which receive tags, attributes, events, values and AF one way
They connect through the gateway to the plant server
They receive daily CSV e-mails only
They cannot use AF at all

explanation: Waterfall replicates PI Data Archive and AF to enterprise replicas through a unidirectional gateway, and users interact normally with the replicas.

prompt: Match each design to OSIsoft's pattern name.

pairs.left: PI Vision, Notifications and Web API in a DMZ
DMZ fed by PI to PI, data only
PI Connector Relay in the DMZ

explanation: These are the security patterns from the PI World 2019 architecture deck. Pattern 2 is Pattern 1 with HA.

prompt: What does Waterfall PI Backfill do?

options.text: Retransmits data to fill gaps without duplicates
Deletes old archives on the replica
Opens a reverse channel for writes
Converts PI tags to OPC UA

explanation: Waterfall PI Backfill retransmits data to fill gaps without duplicates, for example after a link outage.

prompt: True or false: Owl Cyber Defense demonstrated PI to PI replication over its OPDS-1000 data diode.

options.text: True
False

explanation: True. Owl demonstrated "OSI PI to PI Replication" over the OPDS-1000 at the 2018 Barcelona conference.

prompt: What did a 2003 PI conference design use to protect the control network?

options.text: A replica database, with users denied direct access through the firewall and a single secure tunnel out
A data diode with OMF
PI Vision in the control network
AVEVA CONNECT

explanation: The 2003 design used a replica database, denied users direct access and allowed a "single secure tunnel" out. PI Vision, OMF and CONNECT came much later.

prompt: Why do these architectures give business users a replica instead of access to the plant Data Archive? Select all that apply.

options.text: No user query crosses into the control network
A compromised business PC has no path into the plant
It restricts data flow between zones
It removes the need for any authentication on the replica

explanation: Replicas keep user queries and potential attackers out of the control zone and restrict data flow between zones. The replica still needs authentication and hardening.

prompt: Which replication option does Waterfall support for many industrial PI servers?

options.text: Many-to-one aggregation into an enterprise replica, with complete or selective replication
Only one-to-one, with every tag
Two-way synchronisation of all servers
Replication only of AF, not data

explanation: Waterfall supports many-to-one aggregation to an enterprise replica with complete or selective replication.

prompt: A Data Archive placed in a DMZ still needs outbound access for which services, per AVEVA's UC23 firewall table? Select all that apply.

options.text: TCP/UDP 88 for Kerberos
TCP/UDP 135 for SPN registration
UDP 53 for DNS
TCP 3389 for internet RDP

explanation: The UC23 table lists outbound 135 (SPN registration), 88 (Kerberos), 53 (DNS) and dynamic ports to domain controllers. Internet RDP is not part of the PI firewall requirements.
